definition: Workplace robotics safety is an aspect of occupational safety and health when robots are used in the workplace.
details: This includes traditional industrial robots as well as emerging technologies such as drone aircraft and wearable robotic exoskeletons. Types of accidents include collisions, crushing, and injuries from mechanical parts. Hazard controls include physical barriers, good work practices, and proper maintenance.

explainer.lead: Workplace robotics safety covers occupational safety and health when robots are used at work, from industrial arms to drones and wearable exoskeletons. It matters because robot accidents cause collisions, crushing, and mechanical injuries.

tiers.eli5: Robots at work need the same care as heavy machinery: keep people out of the way, follow good habits, and keep the equipment serviced.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply hazard controls such as physical barriers, good work practices, and proper maintenance. Treating robots as just another tool, without barriers or upkeep, is a common pitfall.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the aspect of occupational safety and health concerning robots in the workplace; accident types include collisions, crushing, and injuries from mechanical parts, controlled by barriers, work practices, and maintenance.

explainer.example: A physical barrier around an industrial robot arm keeps workers out of its reach, preventing collision and crushing injuries.
